advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Count a `.json.retired` add in the position map only when the walk saw no `.json` add for that position on a reclaimed history, or document and test that a compaction commit may stand in for a merge-only introduction on ordinary history.
evidence: src/rebar/attest/authorship_resolution.py:186: "--no-merges",
src/rebar/attest/authorship_resolution.py:192: f"*{_RETIRED_SUFFIX}",

src/rebar/attest/authorship_resolution.py:251-253: position = _position_of(path) / if position: / position_map[position] = sha  (a .retired add is mapped even when no .json add for that position was seen)
src/rebar/_commands/compact_txn.py:69: "a miss, an unattributable merge-only event, or a resolver that timed out"
src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py:531-534: if ev.event is None and ev.position: resolved_sha = _resolve_position(ev.position); if resolved_sha is not None: ev.commit_sha = resolved_sha
src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py:218-220: if commit_sha is None and not is_live: return VERIFIED / return KEY_NOT_VALID_AT_ERA

The docstring at authorship_resolution.py:235-237 assumes every event's `.json` add is in the map ('On ordinary history an event's .json add predates the .retired add'). That assumption fails for adds the `--no-merges` walk excludes.
advisory.finding: The batched position map now counts `.json.retired` adds, but the walk uses `--no-merges`. On ordinary (non-reclaimed) history, a compacted event whose `.json` add the walk cannot see (for example a merge-only add, which compact_txn already treats as 'unattributable') now resolves to its later compaction commit instead of missing. The enforced scan then overwrites the ledger's stored commit with that compaction commit and runs the key-era check against it. A key revoked between the event and its compaction now gives `key_not_valid_at_era` and fails the gate, where the unresolved ledger entry used to be accepted through the any-key path.
scenarios: On ordinary history, an event that entered the tracker through a merge commit is later compacted, and its signer's key is revoked between the merge and the compaction. Enforced `verify-identity --all` used to report VERIFIED and now reports key_not_valid_at_era.
`compact --all` sweeps (compact.py:409) now record the compaction commit for such positions in new ledgers instead of an empty marker.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Build both maps in `_batched_resolvers` with a single `authorship.build_event_commit_maps(repo_root=...)` call, so one history walk serves both.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py:441: # Two public builders (each one walk) so tests and callers can substitute either map.
src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py:442-443: commit_map = authorship.build_introducing_commit_map(...) / position_map = authorship.build_position_commit_map(...)
src/rebar/attest/authorship_resolution.py:260: "See :func:`build_event_commit_maps`; callers needing both maps should call it once."
src/rebar/_commands/compact_txn.py:133-134: "on the production store the store-wide walk outran its timeout"
src/rebar/attest/authorship_resolution.py:196: timeout=300 (per walk; a timeout silently yields empty maps and sends every position to the per-position fallback)
advisory.finding: `_batched_resolvers` calls `build_introducing_commit_map` and `build_position_commit_map` separately. Both now wrap the same `build_event_commit_maps` walk, so every enforced run scans the full history twice, and each scan now also lists `.json.retired` paths. This is the same history where, per compact_txn, the store-wide walk already outran its timeout. The new single-walk builder is exported, and its own docstring tells callers needing both maps to call it once.
scenarios: On the 310k-commit tickets history, enforced `verify-identity --all` pays for two full `git log --name-only` walks. If either hits the 300 s timeout, that map comes back empty and the run falls back to one history walk per position.
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace the two builder calls with `commit_map, position_map = authorship.build_event_commit_maps(repo_root=repo_root)`. Tests can monkeypatch `build_event_commit_maps`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `_subprocess_is_ancestor` fail closed for revocation checks (let the exception propagate to `verify_authorship_at_commit`'s outer handler) instead of returning False on every exception
evidence: New code: `except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — ANY git failure → not an ancestor (fail-closed)\n        return False` in `_subprocess_is_ancestor`.
src/rebar/attest/authorship.py:202 `revoked = is_ancestor(revoked_commit, anchor_commit)`: False here means the key is NOT revoked, so returning False on error is permissive for this call.

src/rebar/attest/authorship.py:258-266: the old inline `_is_ancestor` had no try/except, so a TimeoutExpired went to authorship.py:283 `except Exception` and returned `verified=False, verdict="unknown_principal"`.

`_AncestryOracle.__call__` sends a check to `_subprocess_is_ancestor` when the descendant is missing from the `rev-list HEAD` graph. That is reachable for ledger events: verify_authorship.py:528-534 keeps the stored `pos.get("commit_sha")` from snapshot JSON when position resolution misses, and verify_authorship.py:195 passes it as the anchor commit.
advisory.finding: The new fallback `_subprocess_is_ancestor` turns any exception (a 30s TimeoutExpired, an OSError) into False ('not an ancestor'). The era rule also uses this answer for revocation: `revoked = is_ancestor(revoked_commit, anchor_commit)`. So if the merge-base call fails during the revocation check, the key counts as not revoked and stays valid (fail-open). Before this change, the inline `_is_ancestor` in `verify_authorship_at_commit` let the exception reach the outer `except Exception`, which returned a non-verified `unknown_principal` verdict.
scenarios: A snapshot ledger entry carries a stored commit_sha outside HEAD's history (a rewritten or foreign object). The add check succeeds, then the revocation merge-base call times out or hits an OSError, so a revoked key is accepted and the event is marked VERIFIED.
advisory.suggested_fix: In `_subprocess_is_ancestor`, drop the blanket `except Exception: return False` and let TimeoutExpired/OSError propagate, so `verify_authorship_at_commit`'s outer `except Exception` returns the non-verified verdict as it did before. Keep only the `returncode == 0` mapping for normal git exits.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Run the no-merge-base assertion on a multi-commit store where key add commits precede event commits, so `is_ancestor` is actually consulted
evidence: tests/unit/test_verify_identity_reclaim_perf.py:85-86: `root = _git(tracker, "commit-tree", "HEAD^{tree}", "-m", "reclaim checkpoint")` / `_git(tracker, "update-ref", "HEAD", root)` — the history is a single root commit

src/rebar/attest/authorship.py:189-192: `if added_commit == anchor_commit and anchor_position is not None: added = added_at <= anchor_position` / `else: added = is_ancestor(added_commit, anchor_commit)` — is_ancestor only runs when the commits differ
src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py:202: `ev.position,` is always passed as anchor_position, so in a one-commit store every era check takes the position branch
tests/unit/test_verify_identity_reclaim_perf.py:153: `assert merge_bases[0] == 0` — also 0 before the change
advisory.finding: test_enforced_scan_runs_no_merge_base_subprocess_for_era_checks cannot catch a regression in the `is_ancestor` wiring. The reclaimed_store fixture collapses the tracker into ONE root commit, so every keyring add commit equals the event commit. With equal commits, `keys_valid_at_anchor` orders by position and never calls `is_ancestor`. The merge-base count is therefore 0 whether or not the oracle is passed through, and the test passes even if `is_ancestor=is_ancestor` is dropped from `_classify`/`_verify_signed`/`verify_authorship_at_commit`.
scenarios: Someone removes `is_ancestor=is_ancestor` from the `verify_authorship_at_commit` call in `_verify_signed` (verify_authorship.py:205). Enforced `--all` falls back to one merge-base subprocess per keyring record per event, and this test stays green.
advisory.suggested_fix: Build the store with the identity/key added in one commit and signed events in later commits (e.g. the a2c7 `_signed_store` plus extra comments, no history collapse). Assert `merge_bases[0] == 0` and that the scan verified events (rc == 0). Ideally also spy on the oracle to show it was called at least once, so the zero count is not vacuous.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test: cached version present, `ssh-keygen -Y verify` raises FileNotFoundError → verify returns verified=False, verdict=="unavailable"
evidence: src/rebar/attest/sshsig.py:170-175: `except FileNotFoundError: return registry.Verdict(verified=False, verdict="unavailable", ...)` — added lines
src/rebar/attest/sshsig.py:55-56 docstring: `A tool removed after the probe still fails closed, because :meth:`verify` reports a missing ``ssh-keygen`` as ``unavailable``.`

Existing fail-closed tests (tests/unit/test_attest_sshsig.py:184, tests/unit/test_attest_opcert.py:331) patch `ssh_keygen_version` to `None` and so hit the earlier guard at sshsig.py:116, not the new except branch

advisory.finding: The new FileNotFoundError branch in `SshsigScheme.verify` has no test. The commit message says caching the version probe is safe because a missing ssh-keygen at verify time still fails closed as `unavailable`. Named violating input: `ssh_keygen_version()` has cached `(9, 5)`, then `subprocess.run(["ssh-keygen", "-Y", "verify", ...])` raises FileNotFoundError. The expected `Verdict(verified=False, verdict="unavailable")` is never asserted.
scenarios: A refactor drops the try/except. A tool removed after the cached probe then makes verify raise FileNotFoundError instead of returning `unavailable`, and no test fails.
advisory.suggested_fix: Monkeypatch `sshsig.ssh_keygen_version` to `lambda: (9, 5)` and `sshsig.subprocess.run` to raise FileNotFoundError. Call `SshsigScheme().verify(b"x", [dsse.Signature(keyid="p", sig=b"s")], "ns", "")` and assert `v.verified is False and v.verdict == "unavailable"`.

evidence: src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py:457-461: `if position not in looked_up: looked_up[position] = authorship.resolve_position_commit(...)` / `return looked_up[position]` — added lines

advisory.finding: The new memoization in `_batched_resolvers.resolve_position` ("looked up once ... and memoized, hit or miss") has no test. Named violating input: a position absent from `position_map` that is resolved more than once in a run, with `resolve_position_commit` returning `None`. It should call `resolve_position_commit` exactly once. The only related test asserts zero walks, so the memo path never runs.
scenarios: A regression keys the memo on hits only, or skips caching `None`. A keyring position missing from the map then walks the whole history once per event again, which is one of the costs this bug fix removes, and no test fails.
advisory.suggested_fix: Monkeypatch `authorship.build_position_commit_map` to return `{}` and `authorship.resolve_position_commit` to a counting stub returning None. Call `resolve = V._batched_resolvers(tracker, root)[1]` and invoke `resolve("p")` three times. Assert every call returns None and the stub ran once.

advisory.finding: The ancestry oracle's fallback paths are untested. (1) `build_ancestry_oracle` returning `None` when `git rev-list --parents HEAD` fails, e.g. a tracker on an unborn branch with no HEAD commit, after which callers must use merge-base. (2) An ancestor given as a non-40-char abbreviation or ref name that is not in the index, e.g. `oracle(a[:12], d)`, which should go to git and return True. The oracle test only uses full 40-char SHAs and the `"0"*40` sentinel.
scenarios: A change makes the abbreviation path return False the way the full-SHA path does. Keys whose added commits are recorded abbreviated would then be treated as never-added, giving spurious `key_not_valid_at_era`, and no test fails.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_ancestry_oracle_agrees_with_merge_base add `assert oracle(a[:12], d) is _merge_base_says(repo, a[:12], d)`. Add a test that `authorship.build_ancestry_oracle(str(empty_repo))` returns None for a freshly `git init`-ed repo with no commits.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Bind a live event's resolved era commit to its own file's adding commit (the path map) or reject events whose position resolves to a commit other than the one that added their file, before trusting the position map's oldest-add result
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py:356 `position = f"{event.get('timestamp')}-{event.get('uuid')}"`: the position comes from file content.
src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py:188-189 `commit_sha = position_resolver(ev.position or "")` for live events.
New code: `position = _position_of(path)\n        if position:\n            position_map[position] = sha` runs for `.json.retired` paths too, and newest-to-oldest overwrite makes the oldest add win.
src/rebar/attest/authorship_resolution.py:66 the fallback pathspec `f"*{position}-*.json"` never matched `.json.retired`, so before this change these positions did not resolve to the checkpoint.
The new test fixture `reclaimed_store` builds exactly this shape: one root commit that adds compacted events only as `.json.retired`.
dropped.finding: Live events take their era from a position built from their own JSON (`f"{event.get('timestamp')}-{event.get('uuid')}"`), not from their file path or adding commit. The store-wide position map resolves that position to the OLDEST commit that added any file with that position. This change adds `*.json.retired` adds to the map, so on a reclaimed history a newly written event can claim the timestamp and uuid of a compacted event and inherit the reclaim checkpoint commit as its era. Before, those positions missed the map, and the fallback `*{position}-*.json` either found nothing (non-verified) or found the attacker's own later `.json` add.
scenarios: Someone holding a revoked (e.g. leaked) identity key pushes a new event file whose JSON reuses the timestamp/uuid of an event compacted below a reclaim checkpoint. The position resolves to the checkpoint commit, which predates the revocation, so the key counts as valid and the forged event comes out VERIFIED.
